practices.name: Dermal fillers (jaw/chin)
practices.claim: Injecting filler into the jaw and chin instantly gives a sharper, more defined jawline and a stronger profile without surgery.
practices.evidence_rationale: The FDA has approved hyaluronic acid fillers for chin augmentation and, since 2022, one filler for jawline definition, and a systematic review found significant improvement in 17 of 24 chin studies, including four RCTs. Results fade, with global improvement ratings falling from 82-100% early on to 52-77% at 12-18 months.
practices.risk_rationale: Bruising and swelling are common, but an accidental injection into a blood vessel can cause tissue death, vision loss or stroke, and the risk depends on the injector's anatomy knowledge and on whether the product is regulator-approved. In a review covering 2,259 treated chin patients, serious events were rare (one necrosis, one vascular occlusion) and lumps resolved once the filler was dissolved.
key_harms: Blocked blood vessel causing tissue death, vision loss or stroke (rare)
Permanent disfigurement with non-approved permanent fillers such as injectable silicone
practices.safer_alternative: Use a licensed, medically trained injector with a regulator-approved, dissolvable hyaluronic acid filler, and avoid permanent fillers. If the chin or jaw is structurally weak, ask an orthodontist or maxillofacial surgeon whether a lasting fix suits you better.

legal_status.US: FDA-regulated medical devices; approved fillers are indicated for chin augmentation and jawline definition in adults over 21, and use in the nose, forehead and around the eyes is not approved.

practices.name: Fat-dissolving injections (deoxycholic acid, incl. Aqualyx-type products)
practices.claim: Injected 'fat dissolvers' permanently melt chin and jowl fat without surgery.
practices.evidence_rationale: Randomized trials of the single approved deoxycholic acid drug show lasting improvement in under-chin fat, and a trial follow-up found 82% of treated patients still improved at three years. Controlled data cover only that licensed product under the chin; none was found for unapproved fat-dissolving products or for the jowls.
practices.risk_rationale: The FDA reports permanent scars, serious infections, skin deformities and deep painful knots from unapproved fat-dissolving injections, and has logged 129 cases of serious events when the approved drug was used outside the chin, including vision problems and nerve damage. Even under the chin, the approved drug can leave lumps or masses that persist (117 unresolved cases, about 5 months on average).
key_harms: Vision problems when injected near the eyes
practices.safer_alternative: Ask a licensed clinician about the regulator-approved prescription treatment for under-chin fat, which is approved for that area only, and start with supervised weight-management care if the fat is general rather than local. Avoid self-injection and any product bought online.

legal_status.US: Only one deoxycholic acid injection is FDA-approved, for under-chin fat in adults; other fat-dissolving injections are unapproved.
legal_status.AU: A deoxycholic acid injection for under-chin fat in adults is listed as a prescription-only (Schedule 4) medicine.

practices.name: Lateral canthoplasty ('hunter eyes' surgery)
practices.claim: Surgically raising the outer corner of the eye creates a positive canthal tilt ('hunter eyes') that makes the face look more attractive and masculine.
practices.evidence_rationale: Case series show lateral canthal surgery can reposition the outer eyelid corner, but mostly for lid-laxity indications in a mean-age-55 population rather than young men wanting a tilt. The one rating study found (an edited face, 2,081 raters) scored an elevated outer corner lower on attractiveness and masculinity, so nothing supports the cosmetic payoff.
practices.risk_rationale: Even in expert hands, a 600-patient series reported 28 cases of temporary eye-surface swelling, one retrobulbar bleed and 18 repeat operations within two years, and over-tightening can round the corner or pull the lid away from the eye. No safety data were found for cosmetic work on healthy eyes outside specialist oculoplastic practice, and the change cannot be reversed.
key_harms: Bleeding behind the eye (rare, can threaten vision)
Scarring and a permanently altered eye shape
Temporary swelling of the eye surface
practices.safer_alternative: Try non-surgical changes to the eye area first (sleep, sun protection, brow grooming, eyewear choice). If you still want surgery, see an oculoplastic surgeon (an eye surgeon) in your own country and ask frankly what is and isn't reversible.

practices.name: Rhinoplasty
practices.claim: A well-done rhinoplasty permanently reshapes the nose to improve facial harmony and side profile.
practices.evidence_rationale: Evidence is observational: a systematic review reports 72-89% patient satisfaction, and a meta-analysis found facial cosmetic surgery produced no significant self-esteem change (g = 0.23, P = .268). Controlled evidence for the cosmetic result itself is thin.
practices.risk_rationale: Revision rates run about 5-15% and the result is permanent, with a residual hump and tip irregularities the most common complaints. Male patients and people with body dysmorphic disorder, anxiety or depression are more likely to be unhappy even when the surgery is technically sound.
key_harms: Dissatisfaction despite a technically good result
practices.safer_alternative: Choose a surgeon on your country's specialist register who does a lot of nose surgery, ask to be screened for body dysmorphic disorder, get a second opinion, and reassess your goals before booking. Do not use filler as a shortcut, since the FDA lists the nose as an unapproved filler site.

practices.name: Hair transplant abroad (FUE, Turkey)
practices.claim: A cheap, all-inclusive FUE hair transplant in Turkey gives a dense, natural, permanent hairline for a fraction of the home-country price.
practices.evidence_rationale: FUE is the most widely used transplant technique and is reported to give natural-looking results, but the supporting data are uncontrolled series and no controlled trial of transplantation against no treatment was found. Nothing tests the specific claim that high-volume package clinics abroad deliver comparable density and safety.
practices.risk_rationale: The international society of hair restoration surgeons says clinics in Turkey that recruit foreign patients often rely on unlicensed technicians, with depleted donor areas, scarring, unnatural hairlines and infections as the documented results. With qualified surgeons, published reviews put overall FUE complication rates at about 1.2-4.7%, mostly minor and self-limited.
practices.safer_alternative: See a dermatologist first about whether medical treatment should come before surgery, then book a hair-restoration surgeon licensed in your own country and confirm in writing that the surgeon personally makes the incisions and removes the grafts. If you do travel, verify credentials and arrange aftercare before you go.

practices.name: Limb-lengthening surgery
practices.claim: Cosmetic limb-lengthening surgery safely adds several centimetres of permanent height.
practices.evidence_rationale: Two systematic reviews (795 and 760 patients) report average gains of about 6.7 cm and satisfaction of roughly 89-98%, but the first found all included studies were level IV case series or retrospective reviews with no RCTs. Height gain is well documented; the 'safely' part rests on uncontrolled specialist-centre data.
practices.risk_rationale: Even in specialist-centre series, reviews report about 0.15 true complications per patient (new-bone deformity, ankle and subtalar joint stiffness), alongside frequent pin-site infection and ankle equinus, with some nerve injuries and fractures. The reviews do not capture cost-driven overseas clinics, so the as-practiced score is a judgment, not a measured rate.
key_harms: Deformity or fracture of the newly formed bone
practices.safer_alternative: Non-surgical ways to look taller (posture work, tailoring, lifts in footwear) carry far less risk, and a GP or clinical psychologist can help if height distress is significant. If you still pursue surgery, use a specialist limb-reconstruction orthopaedic unit with published outcomes rather than a cosmetic clinic.

proposed.name: Orthognathic (jaw) surgery for cosmetic goals
proposed.why: Often called 'bimax' in the community, it is the legitimate surgical counterpart to bonesmashing and has established clinical indications, so a graded entry would show readers where the evidence-backed route differs from the do-it-yourself one.
